prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1413; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The driver is named on the policy, and the claimant's vehicle was the one struck from behind.
Entry 2: Police report received and reviewed. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact, and it matches the account given by the insured.
Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the repair shop show the rear bumper damage and the point of contact. They confirm some of the details reported, but there are no independent witnesses to the impact itself.
Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records, and nothing suggests the damage occurred before the coverage period began.
Entry 5: Claimant's representing attorney contacted the desk and advised that the claimant has neck and upper back pain consistent with whiplash. Medical records requested.
Entry 6: Medical records reviewed. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records received so far.
Entry 7: The claimant has told the same account of the collision in every conversation with the adjuster and the attorney, with no material changes in the sequence of events.
Entry 8: Repair estimate reviewed. Some of the listed damage appears to be in areas that may not have been affected by this impact, so it is not clear yet whether all of the damage came from this collision. Requested a supplemental inspection.
Entry 9: Treatment records show a usual course of care, with treatment frequency reducing as the claimant's symptoms improved. Treating provider notes indicate steady progress.
Entry 10: File remains open pending the supplemental inspection results and final treatment records. Next review scheduled once those documents are received.
